semantics: Context and Policy must come from host-owned authenticated active-call and live policy state. Parsing caller-supplied records never establishes authority.

A host atomically resolves the live parent scope under the authenticated executor connection, reserves a parent-scoped one-use request_id, and owns cancellation, revocation, disconnect, expiry and uncertain execution. Pure admission does not consume a grant, execute or permit replay.

Delegation compares the authenticated executor with the parent executor and binds both parent scope and parent request. It hashes the actual destination request bytes; hashes are wire-byte identities, not JSON semantic identities.

The live exact destination must appear in both parent and current policy targets. The live policy must bind the same original caller id, kind and issuer as the parent. Its revision must equal the parent revision; changed policy requires a fresh host admission.

Caller id, caller kind, issuer and root scope remain unchanged. Child scope is a fresh host-generated random identity, distinct from parent/root/request identities. The host must also prevent collisions with previous scopes.

Child targets and processing domains are intersections of parent and current policy, deadlines can only shorten, and ancestors/current executor cannot be reentered by changing descriptor revision or version.

Context is sensitive caller metadata, not a bearer credential. Do not log or replicate it, request hashes or scope-derived identities. Provider credentials and host signing keys never enter these records.

Only read and inference execution are eligible. Governed proposal/write effects remain denied even when present in Policy. Parsing never establishes authenticated caller or signed-destination provenance.

The current executor is an effect ceiling: a read executor can delegate only reads; an inference executor can delegate reads or inference. Every read child loses inference targets even if its original caller or parent has broader permission. The inference parent retains its own separately authorized sibling targets.

A Context executor must be read or inference, and every allowed target must fit that executor ceiling. The host attenuates root permission by the exact signed entry-point behavior before creating Context.

Processing permission is independent from inference permission. Destination processing domain must be in the parent/current-policy intersection; an inference grant never implies external-provider consent.

Allowed targets are a host-owned permission snapshot, not a current-capacity catalog. Unrelated readiness changes do not rewrite permission; the host independently verifies actual selected destination/runtime/incarnation and current policy immediately before dispatch.

Independent protocol2 requires a new explicitly negotiated compatible call/installation cohort. Issued composition1/calls1 and portable1 profiles do not accept these records. Profile2 structural admission alone does not qualify native installation, streaming, client identity or provider execution.
The host binds Target behavior and processing_domain to the exact signed destination descriptor; a caller-supplied target, model/task label or annotation never establishes those facts.
